title: Animação — ilha que respira
summary: Uma pequena ilha fantástica com árvores move-se como uma criatura adormecida.
prompt:
CRIA / VIDEO DIRECTION — ANIMAÇÃO — ILHA QUE RESPIRA

DELIVERY
15-second finished video, 16:9, 24fps delivery. The timing describes the final edit; use separate matched clips when the selected generator has a shorter duration limit. Time-lapse compresses the stated real-world interval; slow motion is a dedicated high-speed-imaging treatment.
FRAME COMPOSITION: Native horizontal 16:9 video. Compose the action for this landscape frame; no pillarboxing or letterboxing.

REFERENCES
No external reference is required. Fix the subject design, costume or object design in the first frame and preserve it throughout.

DIRECTION & CINEMATOGRAPHY
Painterly feature-animation with tactile materials, virtual 35mm wide, soft sunrise; ocean and vegetation react to the same displacement.
Use the specific animation or live-action fantasy language stated in DIRECTION. Preserve character design, silhouette and materials. Use clear poses, anticipation, contact, follow-through and a deliberate sense of weight.

SEQUENCE
[0–4s] A lush miniature island floats on a calm fantasy sea, its palms moving gently in the breeze.
[4–10s] The island rises slightly with a deep breath, revealing a huge turtle silhouette beneath the shoreline.
[10–15s] The turtle opens one eye, exhales and slowly swims forward as the trees sway together with its motion.

VFX & CONTINUITY
Houdini-level finish where effects are needed: stable camera tracking, correct occlusion, grounded contact, coherent light direction, reflections and shadows. Couple rigid bodies, cloth, particles, smoke and fluids only when the scene calls for them. Respect mass, momentum and material response around the explicitly fictional event. Do not apply generic glow to every object.
Give each action time to begin, make contact and settle. Use direct cuts for an explicitly different angle or compressed time; keep a continuous shot only where the camera path and geography permit it.

AUDIO
Soft water, foliage, one deep gentle breath and distant birds.
Dialogue is Brazilian Portuguese only where a spoken line is specified. Keep each line within its shot duration. If sound is unsupported by the chosen tool, produce the stated Foley and dialogue separately in post.

FINISH & RESTRICTIONS
Keep subject count, spatial geography, light direction and object ownership consistent. No identity drift, extra fingers, duplicate objects, intersecting surfaces, unmotivated morphs, watermark or burned-in subtitles. Exact lettering, interfaces and planned overlays are composited in post rather than hallucinated by the video model. Preserve any intentional text-based story device in the edit.
